candidate.title: THS-seq
candidate.scope: THS-seq (transposome hypersensitive sites sequencing), the middle, named target row of the assigned Illumina poster crop. The card title, poster row boundaries, and page-118 heading/caption establish this scope. ATAC-seq above, CATCH-IT below, and clipped ORGANIC text at the top are neighboring catalogue rows, not alternatives or material branches of the THS-seq workflow. The five depicted blocks end at a barcoded DNA library; sequencing and analysis are interpreted as the readout, not added as unshown operations. The generic Tn5 label is retained: the paper describes THS-seq implemented with engineered Tn5059 and also evaluates EzTn5, without the poster resolving an enzyme-specific version. The shared architecture does not assert identical complete implementations.

states.label: Open DNA within nucleosome-associated chromatin
features: The exposed linker/accessible DNA is the substrate; nucleosomes remain drawn on flanking DNA.
The label Open DNA does not mean purified naked genomic DNA; the primary paper describes tagmentation of gently lysed cells.

states.label: Tn5 transposome carrying the THS-seq transposon
features: Reagent complex, rather than a specimen-processing intermediate.
The icon labels a read-primer segment and T7 promoter on the transposon.
The paper additionally identifies mosaic-end sequences for transposase binding. The promoter/read-primer oligonucleotide is delivered to genomic DNA; Tn5 supplies enzymatic activity.
The figure names Tn5 generically. The main paper implementation uses Tn5059 and also tests EzTn5; neither enzyme version is uniquely specified by this icon.

features: RNA is a synthetic amplification intermediate made from genomic DNA, rather than endogenous transcripts being measured.
The purple parallel strokes are the IVT-stage product drawing; their layout alone does not establish a duplex molecule.
The paper identifies T7-generated RNA containing genomic insertion-flank sequence that is subsequently converted to cDNA.

evidence.quote: The end sequences of the insertion sites were then linearly amplified with in vitro transcription by roughly 1,000-fold, regardless of the distance between two adjacent Tn5 insertion sites, and the resulting RNA molecules were then converted into sequencing libraries efficiently through seven enzymatic reactions (single-stranded cDNA synthesis, RNase H digestion, double-stranded cDNA synthesis, transposition, protease digestion, end fill-in, and PCR amplification) (Fig. 1).

evidence.locator: [b00010], Interpretation of the RNA-to-library route
evidence.quote: The resulting RNA molecules (Additional file 1: Figure S3a-d) were converted to double-stranded cDNA, followed by a second round of transposition to tag 3’-ends of double-stranded cDNA.
evidence.rationale: RNA is produced by transcription of tagged genomic DNA upstream of this conversion; its cDNA therefore carries genomic insertion-flank information, rather than measuring pre-existing cellular RNA. The late cDNA transposition acts on a copied library substrate, so it does not itself probe chromatin.

states.label: Barcoded DNA sequencing library representing accessible genomic insertion sites
features: Double-stranded DNA with added sequencing-adapter and barcode segments in the terminal schematic.
The paper identifies these as sample-specific DNA barcodes, preserving sample association.
Genomic insertion-flank sequence is the biological information carrier: unique mapped insertion events support chromatin accessibility profiling.
Accessibility is an informative proxy for protein-DNA interactions; the final DNA is not a direct measurement of endogenous RNA or identification of the protein occupying a locus.

Readout limitation: insertion enrichment reflects accessibility with potential transposase sequence bias and off-target transposition; survival into the library does not establish perfect biological specificity.

evidence.locator: [b00014], Results: enzyme comparisons and possible specificity effects
evidence.quote: A higher fraction of overlapping peaks and base pairs between THS-seq and ENCODE reference data indicates that THS-seq not only has a higher sensitivity, but also a higher specificity, which could be due to either less sequence-specific bias or less off-target transposition or both.
evidence.rationale: The paper discusses specificity in terms of sequence bias and off-target transposition; this supports interpreting insertion enrichment as an accessibility proxy with assay-dependent selection, without assuming perfect target specificity.

operations.label: Insert in regions of open chromatin
operations.description: The Tn5 transposome acts on accessible DNA in chromatin, fragmenting/tagging genomic DNA and attaching the promoter/read-primer-bearing transposon at insertion ends.
operations.mechanism: Tn5-catalyzed tagmentation transfers the designed transposon sequences to genomic DNA. Tn5 is the catalyst within the reagent complex, while its loaded transposon contributes attached DNA.
operations.information_effect: Physical linkage of library-compatible sequence and a T7 promoter to a genomic insertion flank makes accessible DNA ends recoverable in the later amplification and library. Insertion reports transposome access under this assay.

operations.label: End fill-in and IVT amplification
operations.description: The tagged DNA undergoes end/gap fill-in and serves as the template for T7-driven in vitro transcription, producing amplified RNA copies of accessible genomic end sequences.
operations.mechanism: The paper describes DNA polymerase gap fill-in followed by T7 RNA polymerase transcription from the inserted promoter. The two actions remain one operation at the figure's combined-block scope.
operations.information_effect: Linear RNA amplification copies genomic end sequences adjacent to insertions. The paper reports this can recover insertion ends without the distance dependence of directly PCR-amplifying the region between two adjacent initial insertion sites.

method_scopes.rationale: All five operations lie in the independently labeled THS-seq row, match the schematic under the page-118 THS-seq heading, and are supported by Sos et al. full text. The transposome is an added reagent, and the leftmost yellow-highlighted chromatin cartoon describes the target rather than a separate processing branch. Neither neighboring row supplies an operation or target alternative. The Tn5059/EzTn5 comparisons in the paper do not add an unshown alternative workflow target.

checks.rationale: Accept at the declared Illumina THS-seq schematic scope. Independent image inspection and targeted full-text reads support every state, all five local operations and all eleven routes. The promoter-tagged chromatin to purified DNA to IVT RNA to ds cDNA to sample-barcoded DNA chain has consistent interfaces. The initial two-input operation joins chromatin substrate with a loaded reagent complex; there are no independent sample branches collapsed into it. All depicted THS-seq transformations are retained, and neighboring rows are excluded. The paper resolves the RNA carrier, protein removal and late cDNA tagging without requiring a contrary source correction.
